title: A Promise for the Kitchen
premise: Ada Delacroix built her wedding-planning empire on the ruins of her own abandoned marriage, and she no longer believes in the vows she sells. When her sister's reunion threatens to expose how badly Ada's life has frayed, she recruits Theo Marchetti — a disgraced former prosecutor turned line cook who once put her brother-in-law's business under investigation — to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but their pasts collide: Theo is quietly building a case that could destroy the family venue Ada depends on, and Ada discovers he has been using her client list as evidence. As the harvest festival approaches, both must choose between the careers that saved them and a love that demands the truth; in the end, Theo withdraws his testimony, Ada testifies on her own terms, and they open a small supper club together where every promise is kept at a kitchen table instead of an altar.
about_author: Noor Halloran spent a decade catering weddings before trading her clipboard for a writing desk, and her fiction still smells faintly of burnt sugar and rain. She lives in a coastal town where the festivals are loud, the kitchens are louder, and second chances arrive unfashionably late.

chapters.title: The Cake She Never Cut
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At a lavish wedding she planned flawlessly, Ada watches the bride cry and feels nothing but old scar tissue, remembering her own canceled ceremony ten years ago. Her assistant notices her hands shaking over the cake knife. Emotional beat: grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Summons from the Family Table
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A group text from her mother announces the Delacroix family reunion during the harvest festival, with pointed questions about who Ada will bring. Her sister Margot calls to warn her that Aunt Renée plans an intervention about Ada being 'alone and difficult.' Beat: dread wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: The Man Who Burns Things Beautifully
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the kitchen of Braise, Theo torches a crème brûlée while mentally reviewing the whistleblower file hidden in his locker — evidence against the Verrone hospitality group, which owns half the town including the Delacroix venue. His old law partner texts: the window to file closes after the festival. Beat: quiet obsession.

chapters.title: A Transaction Over Coffee
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada finds Theo at the farmers market and, on impulse born of desperation, offers him money to be her date for the reunion weekend. He refuses payment but agrees anyway, which unsettles them both. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Over wine, they draft fake-relationship rules: no real names of exes, no touching without warning, leave Sunday night separately. Theo breaks rule three immediately by walking her home. Beat: flirtation wearing armor.

chapters.title: The Reunion Begins
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo meets the Delacroix clan at Margot's farmhouse and is startled by how warm it is — his own family dinners were crime-scene silences. Aunt Renée interrogates him; Ada's hand finds his under the table, unbidden. Beat: belonging he didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. After dinner, Ada and Theo slow-dance in the kitchen to a broken radio, and the performance dissolves — a kiss neither planned. Ada pulls away first, terrified. Beat: the fake becomes true and neither admits it.

chapters.title: What Theo Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone, Theo reviews the Verrone file and realizes the Delacroix venue lease is entangled with the corruption he's chasing. Filing means Ada's family business could collapse. He tells himself the truth can be managed. Beat: the first real lie between them.

chapters.title: Sunday Escape
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They slip out of the reunion early and drive to the coast, eating gas-station sandwiches. Ada almost tells him about her failed marriage; instead she invents a version where she was the one left. Beat: intimacy built on a small betrayal.

chapters.title: The Client List
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo cross-references Ada's wedding clients against Verrone shell companies and finds a pattern only her planner logs reveal. He copies a page, hating himself. Beat: complicity deepening.

chapters.title: Margot Suspects
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot confronts Ada: 'He looks at you like you're real. So why does he flinch when someone mentions the venue?' Ada deflects, but the question lodges. Beat: the audience sees what Ada won't.

chapters.title: Festival Preparations
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town preps for the harvest festival; Ada is hired to plan the festival gala, putting her and Theo in constant proximity. Their banter sharpens into shorthand, into ease. Beat: falling in love disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: An Old Ring
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Packing for the gala, Ada finds her unworn engagement ring and remembers Daniel, who chose his career over their wedding day. She wonders if she's now doing the same thing in reverse. Beat: history rhyming.

chapters.title: The Prosecutor's Ghost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a bar, Theo runs into his former mentor, Judge Okafor, who warns him: 'You're not pursuing justice anymore, you're pursuing a verdict. Know the difference.' Theo doesn't answer. Beat: conscience knocking.

chapters.title: First Real Fight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. When Ada mentions the venue's expansion deal, Theo goes rigid and accuses her of defending corrupt people. Ada, stung, accuses him of judging a family he's known for two weeks. Beat: the truth leaking through the cracks.

chapters.title: Apology in Flour
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo shows up at Ada's office with bread he baked at 4 a.m. and no adequate explanation. She lets him help her build a gingerbread model of the gala tent. Beat: forgiveness offered before honesty earned.

chapters.title: Aunt Renée's Wisdom
chapters.summary: Renée's POV. Renée corners Ada at the bakery and reveals she once loved a man who lied to protect her, and it cost her thirty years. 'Love isn't the risk, child. It's the rescue mission you run for someone who won't tell you where they're bleeding.' Beat: thematic key delivered gently.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower Calls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's source inside Verrone panics — there's a mole hunt, and the trail points toward anyone with venue access. Theo must move fast or bury the file. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Gala Night, Part One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The festival gala opens beautifully; Ada, radiant in command, dances with Theo in front of the whole town. Her mother whispers, 'Keep this one.' Beat: peak of the false golden hour.

chapters.title: Gala Night, Part Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During the toast, a Verrone lawyer recognizes Theo and loudly recalls his disbarment-adjacent scandal. The room turns. Ada realizes she knows almost nothing about why he left the law. Beat: public crack in the facade.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada demands answers; Theo gives her a partial truth — he was pushed out for investigating powerful people — and omits that her family is in the file. She accepts it because she wants to. Beat: chosen blindness.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot, doing venue paperwork, finds a copied page of Delacroix client records in the gala office and assumes Ada leaked them. Family trust fractures. Beat: misunderstanding as time bomb.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Venue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Margot accuses Ada publicly; Theo steps in to defend her and nearly reveals too much. Ada watches him lie smoothly to her sister and feels ice: he's good at this. Too good. Beat: love and doubt holding hands.

chapters.title: Daniel Returns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada's ex-fiancé Daniel appears at the festival as a Verrone consultant — and he recognizes Theo from the old investigation. He warns Ada, smiling: 'Ask him what he's really here for.' Beat: the past weaponized.

chapters.title: What the File Contains
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered by Daniel, Theo reads the full file and learns the Verrone scheme deliberately targeted the Delacroix lease all along — Ada's family was always the mark. Filing saves strangers and ruins the woman he loves. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Discovery
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds the copied page and the file in Theo's festival lodging. Every kindness re-reads as reconnaissance. She leaves without a word, taking the file with her. Beat: heartbreak as evidence.

chapters.title: Two Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Split POV. Ada sits alone in the closed venue; Theo stands outside in the rain, unable to knock. Both rehearse speeches the other will never hear. Beat: parallel solitude.

chapters.title: Sister's Court
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot reads the file herself and realizes the leak wasn't Ada — it was theft aimed at them. She also realizes Theo filed nothing yet. 'He still has a choice,' she tells Ada. 'So do you.' Beat: alliance rebuilt through anger.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel offers Theo reinstatement, a clean record, and a promotion if he hands over the file and walks away. It's everything Theo lost, priced exactly at Ada. Beat: temptation with a bow on it.

chapters.title: Kitchen Confession
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds Ada at the venue kitchen at midnight, prepping stress-batch pastry. He confesses everything: the file, the copied page, the moment he stopped investigating her and started loving her. He doesn't ask forgiveness. Beat: naked truth at last.

chapters.title: Ada Decides
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada weighs loyalty to family, justice for the other families Verrone ruined, and the man who chose truth too late. She bakes until dawn and reaches a decision the reader doesn't see. Beat: the fulcrum.

chapters.title: Her Terms
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada summons Theo and Okafor: she'll return the file and testify about the venue records herself — on the condition the Delacroix lease is protected and Theo files before the festival ends. Justice, but outside the safe channels. Beat: agency seized.

chapters.title: Filing Day
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo submits the case with Ada beside him, then refuses Daniel's offer publicly, burning his bridge back to the law. Walking out, he feels lighter than he has in years. Beat: sacrifice completed.

chapters.title: Verrone Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Verrone retaliates: the gala is threatened with cancellation, Ada's business license is challenged, and Daniel leaks the fake-dating story to humiliate her. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Town Rallies
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Margot, Renée, the festival committee, even rival planners defend Ada; vendors volunteer for the gala. Theo cooks for the whole crew. Love shown as community, not just romance. Beat: warmth against pressure.

chapters.title: Hearing Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the emergency licensing hearing, Ada speaks plainly about what was done to her family and others. Okafor rules in her favor and signals the Verrone case will proceed. Beat: justice earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Grand Gesture, Undone
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo plans a grand romantic gesture, then throws it away, realizing Ada deserves a conversation, not a performance. He asks for nothing — only to cook beside her again someday. Beat: humility as romance.

chapters.title: Festival's Last Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Under the festival lanterns, Ada finds Theo at a small pop-up supper club he built with their friends. No speech, no crowd — just two chairs, one table, and an honest question. She says yes to dinner, and to trying. Beat: climax resolved in quiet.

chapters.title: A Promise for the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, the Verrone executives are indicted; the Delacroix venue thrives. Ada and Theo sign a lease on a tiny storefront: a supper club called Promise, where couples eat before deciding to marry — or not. Beat: new tradition, healed belief.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Second Helpings
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. One year later at the harvest festival, Margot teases, Renée approves, and Theo proposes nothing — instead handing Ada a menu whose dessert is named 'For Ada, Who Saw Clearly First.' She laughs, kisses him, and rings the service bell. Beat: joy without an altar.
